found.domain_assessment:
METHOD CAVEAT FIRST. This finder ran with zero WebSearch capacity (the session budget of 200 searches was exhausted before it started; every one of my 8 initial queries returned 'budget used') and an egress allowlist that admitted only github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com. Every regulator, court, statistics, academic, archive and vendor host I tried (dol.gov, gao.gov, eeoc.gov, ecfr.gov, uscourts.gov, federalregister.gov, acquisition.gov, sam.gov, madeinamerica.gov, mspb.gov, eur-lex, TED, single-market-scoreboard, legifrance, economie.gouv.fr, fairwork.gov.au, gov.uk, archive.org, hal.science, core.ac.uk, semanticscholar, ssrn, nber, ncbi, servicenow, adp, ramp, navan, expensify.com, shrm, oecd, wikipedia) was blocked. The GitHub REST search API also returned 502/503 for most queries. So the 'at least 10 searches, 5 fetches' requirement was met only on the fetch side (about 20 GitHub-hosted sources fetched). Operational volumes (case counts, appeal rates, cost per review) for the US and EU workflows could NOT be verified this session; where I give them they are recalled figures flagged 'unverified', each with the primary URL where the parent should confirm them. Absence of verified data below is uncertainty, not evidence.

WHAT THE FETCHED EVIDENCE DOES SHOW. (1) The clearest settlement-loop artefact in this cluster is state-owned, not employer-owned: France's Code du travail numérique, published by the Direction générale du Travail, maintains 'contributions' = recurring HR/labour-law questions with a generic answer plus per-convention-collective answers, each carrying legi/kali legal references, an answer content-type (ANSWER, NOTHING, CDT, UNFAVOURABLE, UNKNOWN, SP, GENERIC_NO_CDT), a status pipeline REDACTING->REDACTED->VALIDATING->VALIDATED->PUBLISHED with user_id and timestamp, and Publicodes executable models (préavis, indemnité de licenciement) per agreement. That is typed, versioned, provenance-bearing, prospective settlement of repeatable ambiguity (category H) at national scale, but (a) the owner is the regulator, (b) it is informational rather than binding on tribunals, (c) it is free. It is evidence that the mechanism is real and also that where it exists the natural owner is the rule-maker, which undercuts an employer-side standalone product in France. (2) Rules-as-code projects that encode French social law (OpenFisca-France, Urssaf mon-entreprise/modele-social, Catala examples, DGFiP's M language) record interpretive settlements as code comments citing a circulaire, a CAF web page or an undated ministry PDF, with explicit 'Hypothèses/points à éclaircir' notes: the interpretations ARE captured, but provenance and versioning are informal. That supports H3 partially (organisations do encode settled interpretations) and shows the residual gap is governance/provenance, which is small and cheap to fill in-house. (3) The FAR mirror shows federal procurement rules are versioned by Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC 2025-06, 1 Oct 2025), and the regime itself mandates written, tiered-approval, publicly posted justifications for sole-source awards and numbered agency class deviations: the settlement loop is already institutionalised in law and in contract-writing systems, and the per-acquisition justification is case-specific (G/E), so procurement scores weak for H. (4) Expensify's own docs confirm the expense control model is limits + auto-approve compliant reports (default $100 threshold on Collect) + random audit + category approvers, i.e. bright lines and sampling, consistent with the prior IPSA finding that expenses fail the economics. (5) DOL's open-source timesheet tool computes overtime arithmetic only and explicitly excludes classification/exemption questions, which is where the payroll ambiguity lives.

WHERE THE STRUCTURE IS MOST SOPHON-SHAPED (unverified volumes). ERISA benefit claims: 29 CFR 2560.503-1(b)(5) requires plan claims procedures to include safeguards ensuring 'plan provisions have been applied consistently with respect to similarly situated claimants', (g) requires disclosure of any internal rule, guideline or protocol relied on, and appeals must be decided by a different fiduciary without deference. That is a regulatory mandate for exactly the recorded, reusable, provenance-bearing settlement the brief describes, with a clear owner (plan administrator / named fiduciary) and an audit trail requirement. But the adjudication is mostly outsourced to insurers/TPAs whose claim platforms already hold the 'internal guidelines', and a human fiduciary must remain on every appeal (H4). Australian modern-award interpretation is the payroll sub-domain with the largest documented error cost (hundreds of millions of AUD in self-reported corporate underpayments; FWO recoveries in the A$400-500m/yr range, unverified) and genuinely repeatable interpretive ambiguity, but the settlements are made by the Fair Work Commission/Ombudsman and courts, not the employer, and are consumed as payroll configuration changes.

OVERALL: weak-to-uncertain for a standalone product in this cluster. Expenses and procurement exceptions are negative/weak. HR tier-2 and payroll are dominated by missing evidence, factual classification and legal-risk discretion, with the H-shaped residue settled upstream by regulators and then encoded in HRIS/payroll configuration or knowledge articles. The one candidate worth an empirical base-rate test is benefit claim appeals at a self-administered plan or TPA (count how many appeal reversals turn on a plan-language interpretation that then recurs), and the one public corpus that could be mined cheaply for recurrence is the CDTN contributions set (SocialGouv/cdtn-admin), which already exists on GitHub.

workflows.name: HR policy interpretation: leave eligibility, accommodations, FMLA/ADA determinations, disciplinary consistency, HR tier-2 escalations
workflows.geography: US (FMLA/ADA, federal-sector discipline) and France (Code du travail, conventions collectives)
workflows.decision_volume: UNVERIFIED (hosts blocked). US: FMLA leave-taking about 15% of covered employees in a 12-month period per DOL 2018 Employer/Employee survey, https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fmla/2018-survey-results (government statistics; recalled, not fetched). EEOC charges: roughly 81,000 (FY2023) to 88,500 (FY2024) total, of which disability charges are on the order of a third, https://www.eeoc.gov/data/charge-statistics-charges-filed-eeoc-fy-1997-through-fy-2024 (regulator; recalled, unverified). Federal-sector discipline appeals to MSPB on the order of 5,000-6,000 per year, https://www.mspb.gov/publicaffairs/annual_reports.htm (tribunal; recalled, unverified). France: no volume retrieved; CDTN tracks monthly page views per contribution via Matomo but publishes no count in the repo, https://github.com/SocialGouv/cdtn-admin/blob/master/analysis/src/analysis/reports/contrib_monthly_views.py (government repo, fetched). ServiceNow HRSD / Workday Help tier-2 shares: NOT FOUND (docs.servicenow.com blocked).
workflows.human_review_rate: Not sourced. FMLA and ADA determinations are 100% human-touched by design (interactive process, certification review); tier-2 HR case share unknown. Basis: process structure only; no operational data reachable this session.
workflows.why_humans_review: Estimate, basis = structure of the processes plus the CDTN answer taxonomy, no case-level data: A missing evidence 25-35% (medical certification, hours-worked eligibility facts); B factual classification 15-20% (serious health condition, essential functions, 'similar offence'); C interpretation of existing rule 10-15%; D conflict of authorities 5-10% (state vs federal leave, convention collective vs Code du travail, the CDTN even has content types NOTHING/CDT/UNFAVOURABLE for exactly this); E true discretion 15-25% (undue hardship, penalty selection, legal-risk judgement); F 0-5%; G 5%; H repeatable ambiguity settled prospectively 10-15%. The H share is real (the DGT publishes per-convention settled answers precisely because employers ask the same questions repeatedly) but in the private employer the H residue is small once the regulator's answer exists.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Code du travail numérique (code.travail.gouv.fr), edited by the Direction générale du Travail (director of publication: the Directeur général du Travail), maintains 'contributions': recurring labour-law questions with a generic answer and per-convention-collective answers, each with legi (Code) and kali (collective agreement) references, an answer type (ANSWER, NOTHING, CDT, UNFAVOURABLE, UNKNOWN, SP, GENERIC_NO_CDT), and a governed status pipeline REDACTING->REDACTED->VALIDATING->VALIDATED->PUBLISHED with user_id and created_at audit rows.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Published answers are reused by every employer/employee consulting the same question for the same agreement; Publicodes models (préavis, indemnité de licenciement per convention) make the settled reading executable. Informational, not binding on courts; owner is the regulator, not the employer.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Answer editor exposes explicit content types for the conflict-of-authorities case ('La convention collective renvoie au Code du Travail', 'est intégralement moins favorable que le CDT', 'ne prévoit rien') and a message block for untreated agreements: the ministry is settling D-type conflicts prospectively per agreement.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Answer applies to all later queries for that agreement until re-validated; legal-change alerts (targets/alert-cli) trigger review.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Publicodes README lists Code du travail numérique (layoff compensation and notice-period simulators) and Urssaf mon-entreprise as production users of executable public-interest rules.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Rules are versioned in git and re-executed for every user; settlement is encoded as a rule, which is the H3 pattern (organisations already encode settled interpretations).

settlement_loop_evidence.description: US federal-sector discipline: Douglas v. Veterans Administration, 5 M.S.P.R. 280 (1981) makes 'consistency of the penalty with those imposed upon other employees for the same or similar offenses' a mandatory factor and agencies maintain tables of penalties; MSPB reviews penalty consistency on appeal.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Tables of penalties are prospective, versioned agency documents; prior penalties for similar offences are cited as precedent in later cases. Volume and reversal rates not verified.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Legal notices of the CDTN site: 'Le site est édité par la Direction générale du Travail, au sein du Ministère du Travail...' (publisher named), confirming the settlement owner is the national rule-maker.

workflows.economic_pain: UNVERIFIED. Cost of inconsistency shows up as discrimination/retaliation charges and FMLA interference suits (EEOC charge counts above; DOL WHD FMLA back-wage recoveries at https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/data/charts/overall-enforcement-statistics, blocked). No cost-per-HR-case or tier-2 headcount figure could be retrieved (ServiceNow/Workday/Gartner hosts blocked). SHRM data on policy inconsistency: NOT FOUND (shrm.org blocked).
workflows.existing_solutions: ServiceNow HRSD and Workday Help (case + knowledge articles; resolved cases become knowledge articles, not typed executable settlements), leave-administration TPAs and vendors (AbsenceSoft, Cocoon, Tilt, Sparrow: eligibility rules configured, not precedent ledgers), accommodation platforms (Disclo, Inclusively), employment counsel. In France the state itself supplies the settlement corpus free (CDTN) and Publicodes/OpenFisca encode it. None found that records employer-level interpretations as versioned executable precedents with who/when/what-power (consistent with prior finding).
workflows.buyer_and_budget: HR shared-services / HR operations leader, or Leave & Accommodations manager in large employers; legal/employment counsel as veto holder. Budget exists (HRSD licences) but sits with the case-management incumbent; a standalone precedent ledger would be a feature request to ServiceNow/Workday.
workflows.regulatory_constraints: FMLA/ADA require individualised assessment and an interactive process (ADA), so a human must remain on every accommodation decision (H4); GDPR/health-data handling for medical certification; France: convention collective hierarchy and prud'hommes review; automated decision-making limits (GDPR Art. 22) for adverse HR outcomes in the EU.
workflows.notes: Strongest artefact: a national regulator already runs a typed, versioned, per-agreement settlement corpus (CDTN). That validates the mechanism's shape but points to the regulator, not the employer, as the natural owner; employer-side H residue after the regulator's answer is small. Volumes and tier-2 shares remain unmeasured.

workflows.name: Payroll exceptions: overtime/exemption classification, garnishments, retro pay, error correction
workflows.geography: US (FLSA), Australia (modern awards) as the high-loss comparator, France (Urssaf cotisations)
workflows.decision_volume: UNVERIFIED. US WHD back wages on the order of $270-280M per year for ~150-165k workers in FY2023-24, https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/data/charts/overall-enforcement-statistics (regulator; recalled, blocked). Garnishment incidence about 7% of US employees (ADP Research Institute 2017), https://www.adp.com/resources/articles-and-insights/articles/t/the-us-wage-garnishment-landscape.aspx (vendor research; recalled, blocked). Australia: Fair Work Ombudsman recovered roughly A$470M for ~160k workers in 2023-24, https://www.fairwork.gov.au/about-us/access-accountability-and-reporting/annual-reports (regulator; recalled, blocked). Payroll error cost: EY 2017 study often cited as ~15 errors per pay period and ~$291 per correction, vendor/consultancy, URL not retrievable, UNVERIFIED. Off-cycle payment shares: NOT FOUND.
workflows.human_review_rate: Not sourced. Structure: the arithmetic (overtime at 1.5x over 40 hours, garnishment limits) is fully deterministic and automated; DOL's own open-source timesheet calculator does arithmetic only and 'does not handle' tips, bonuses, deductions, shift differentials and does not address exemption status, https://github.com/USDepartmentofLabor/DOL-Timesheet (government repo, fetched). Human review concentrates on classification (exempt/non-exempt, award coverage, regular-rate inclusions) and on garnishment order interpretation.
workflows.why_humans_review: Estimate, basis = process structure and the Australian remediation pattern: A missing evidence 20-30% (hours records, order documents); B factual classification 30-40% (duties test, award classification level, allowance eligibility); C rule interpretation 10-15% (what enters the regular rate, annualised-salary reconciliation); D conflict of authorities 5-10% (state vs federal, multiple garnishment orders' priority); E discretion 5%; F 0%; G 5%; H repeatable ambiguity settled prospectively 10-20%. The H component is real in Australia (award interpretation errors repeated across thousands of employees for years) but is settled by the Fair Work Commission/Ombudsman/courts and then consumed as payroll configuration.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: US WHD opinion letters: an employer asks the Administrator to rule on a fact pattern; the letter is numbered, dated, can be withdrawn, and gives a good-faith reliance defence under the Portal-to-Portal Act (29 U.S.C. 259). Regulator-level prospective settlement of repeatable classification ambiguity.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Other employers with materially identical facts rely on the letter; settlement is external to the firm and consumed as a payroll rule change.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Urssaf's mon-entreprise encodes French cotisations in Publicodes ('règles de calcul des cotisations sociales, des impôts et des droits sociaux' used on mon-entreprise.urssaf.fr); the rule base is versioned in git and reusable by third parties.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Settled readings become executable rules published by the collecting agency; supports H3 (already encoded) for the French payroll case.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: OpenFisca-France housing-benefit module cites 'circulaire interministérielle DSS/2B n°2011-447 du 01/12/2011', a 2011 CAF web page and a 2016 ministry PDF as sources for specific rule readings, with a code comment 'Hypothèses/points à éclaircir' listing unresolved ambiguities.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Interpretations are captured as executable rules, but provenance is a free-text comment: shows the capture happens and the governance gap is modest.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Australian large-employer underpayment remediations (e.g., Woolworths, litigated by the FWO over annualised-salary reconciliation under the Retail Award) are the largest documented cost of unsettled award interpretation repeated across a workforce.
settlement_loop_evidence.source_type: regulator (recalled; blocked, not fetched; amounts unverified)
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Court/FWC findings on award meaning are prospective for all employers under the award; employer-side fix is payroll configuration and back-pay, not a precedent ledger.

workflows.economic_pain: Large but concentrated in wrong classification rather than case-by-case review: US WHD and private FLSA collective actions (US district court FLSA filings in Table C-2, https://www.uscourts.gov/data-news/data-tables, blocked, unverified) and Australian remediation in the hundreds of millions of AUD (unverified). Per-exception review cost not sourced.
workflows.existing_solutions: Payroll engines (ADP, Workday, SAP SuccessFactors EC Payroll, UKG, Dayforce) with configurable earnings/exemption codes; garnishment services (ADP Wage Garnishment); award-interpretation engines in Australia (Tanda, Deputy, Rippling AU, KeyPay) that encode award readings as configuration; regulator opinion letters and FWO/FWC guidance. None found that keeps employer-level interpretations as versioned typed precedents; configuration change logs partially serve that role.
workflows.buyer_and_budget: Payroll manager / payroll compliance lead; general counsel for classification. Budget sits with the payroll platform and award-interpretation vendors.
workflows.regulatory_constraints: Employer remains liable for misclassification regardless of tooling; opinion-letter reliance requires identical facts; Australia's criminal wage-theft provisions (from 2025) raise the cost of wrong settlement and push decisions to counsel (H4).
workflows.notes: The high-cost ambiguity is settled upstream by regulators/courts and lands as configuration; residual employer-level H volume is unmeasured and likely small per employer. Australian award interpretation is the sub-domain to check if the parent wants a payroll wedge.

workflows.name: Benefits administration: ERISA claims and appeals, plan document interpretation, plan administrator discretion
workflows.decision_volume: UNVERIFIED. EBSA Benefits Advisors closed on the order of 200,000 participant inquiries in FY2023 and recovered roughly $444M through informal complaint resolution (total EBSA monetary results ~ $1.4B), https://www.dol.gov/agencies/ebsa/about-ebsa/our-activities/resource-center/fact-sheets/ebsa-monetary-results (regulator; recalled, blocked). ERISA civil filings in US district courts on the order of 7,000-9,000 per year (nature-of-suit 791), https://www.uscourts.gov/data-news/data-tables (court statistics; recalled, blocked). Plan-level claim and appeal counts: NOT FOUND; the 2016 disability claims rule RIA at https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2016/12/19/2016-29353/claims-procedure-for-plans-providing-disability-benefits holds DOL's estimates (blocked).
workflows.human_review_rate: By regulation every appeal is reviewed by a named fiduciary who did not make the initial decision and gives no deference to it (29 CFR 2560.503-1(h)(3)(ii)); initial claims are largely auto-adjudicated by insurer/TPA systems, appeals are 100% human. Basis: regulation text (recalled; ecfr.gov and law.cornell.edu blocked).
workflows.why_humans_review: Estimate, basis = the regulation's own required-content list for denials (specific plan provision relied on; internal rule/guideline/protocol relied on; additional material needed) and the appeal structure: A missing evidence 30-40% (the denial notice must state what additional material would perfect the claim); B factual classification 20-25% (medical necessity, disability definition met, eligibility class); C rule interpretation 10-15% (plan-language meaning); D conflict of authorities 5% (plan document vs SPD vs insurer guideline); E discretion 10-15% (Firestone discretionary authority, exercised but reviewable); F 0%; G 5%; H repeatable ambiguity settled prospectively 10-15%. The H share is structurally supported because (b)(5) requires consistency with similarly situated claimants and (g) requires disclosing the internal rule relied on, which forces plans to hold reusable interpretations.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: 29 CFR 2560.503-1(b)(5): plan claims procedures must 'contain administrative processes and safeguards designed to ensure and to verify that benefit claim determinations are made in accordance with governing plan documents and that, where appropriate, the plan provisions have been applied consistently with respect to similarly situated claimants.' Denials must identify the specific plan provision and any internal rule, guideline, protocol or similar criterion relied on (or state it is available on request).
settlement_loop_evidence.source_type: regulator (regulation text recalled; host blocked, not fetched)
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: The regulation itself mandates a reusable, disclosable interpretation ('internal rule, guideline, protocol') applied consistently to later similar claimants: the settlement loop is a legal requirement, and the artefact (the internal guideline) is exactly what the brief calls a captured settlement.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Firestone Tire & Rubber Co. v. Bruch, 489 U.S. 101 (1989): where the plan grants the administrator discretionary authority to determine eligibility or construe terms, courts review interpretations deferentially; the plan administrator is therefore the authoritative interpreter, and its prior interpretations of the same term are evidence of consistent (non-arbitrary) administration.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Clear institutional owner (plan administrator / named fiduciary) whose settlement is authoritative subject to arbitrary-and-capricious review; inconsistency with prior interpretations is a classic ground for reversal, which is the economic reason to keep a precedent ledger.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Appeals must be decided by an appropriate named fiduciary who is neither the initial decision-maker nor their subordinate, without deference, within 60 days (45 for disability, 30/15 for health post-/pre-service), with the claimant entitled to all documents relevant to the claim.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Case-specific; establishes that a human must remain on every appeal (H4), so the product value is in faster, consistent, better-documented appeals rather than removing the human.

workflows.economic_pain: UNVERIFIED but structurally large: informal EBSA recoveries in the hundreds of millions per year, ERISA litigation in the thousands of cases per year, fee-shifting under ERISA 502(g), and reversal risk from inconsistent interpretation. Cost per appeal review and TPA headcount: NOT FOUND.
workflows.existing_solutions: Insurer and TPA claim platforms (e.g., FINEOS for disability, health-plan adjudication systems, benefit-administration platforms such as Alight, bswift, Businessolver), plan-document/SPD generation vendors, ERISA counsel; the 'internal rules, guidelines, protocols' the regulation refers to live as clinical policy bulletins and claim manuals (versioned documents, not typed executable precedents linked to decisions). Consistency verification is usually audit sampling. No vendor found that links appeal outcomes to a versioned interpretation of a plan term and re-applies it automatically.
workflows.buyer_and_budget: Plan administrator at a large self-insured employer, or the appeals/quality function at a TPA or disability insurer; budget exists (compliance, litigation avoidance) but the appeals unit is inside the claims platform's remit.
workflows.regulatory_constraints: Human named fiduciary must decide every appeal; full and fair review and disclosure duties; deference depends on plan language; state insurance law overlays for insured plans; no rule prohibits using a precedent ledger to draft or check decisions.
workflows.notes: Best structural fit in this cluster: a regulation that literally requires consistent application to similarly situated claimants and disclosure of the internal rule relied on, plus a clear owner. Missing: any verified count of appeals, share reversed on interpretation grounds, or recurrence of the same plan-term ambiguity. This is the workflow to run the brief's 100-500 case base-rate experiment on, at a self-administered plan or TPA appeals unit.

workflows.name: Procurement exceptions: sole-source justifications (FAR 6.302/J&A), individual and class deviations (FAR 1.4), Buy American waivers, EU Art. 32 negotiated procedure without publication, French below-threshold and 'sans publicité' purchases, exception logs
workflows.decision_volume: UNVERIFIED. US: roughly one-third of federal contract obligations are not competed (GAO/USAspending competition data; DoD competition rate around half), https://www.gao.gov (blocked), https://www.acq.osd.mil/dpap/cpic/cp/competition_report.html (blocked); GAO bid protests about 1,800 filed in FY2024 with sustain rate ~16% and effectiveness rate ~52%, https://www.gao.gov/legal/bid-protests/bid-protest-annual-reports (audit body; recalled, blocked). DoD class deviations: a few dozen numbered deviations per year, https://www.acq.osd.mil/dpap/dars/class_deviations.html (blocked). Buy American waivers posted individually for public comment at https://www.madeinamerica.gov/waivers/ (blocked). EU: single-bidder and no-call-for-bids shares in the Single Market Scoreboard, https://single-market-scoreboard.ec.europa.eu/policy_areas/public-procurement_en (blocked, not recalled with confidence). France: OECP recensement annual counts at https://www.economie.gouv.fr/daj/recensement-economique-commande-publique (blocked, not recalled with confidence).
workflows.human_review_rate: 100% by construction: every other-than-full-and-open award requires a written justification, certified by the contracting officer and approved at dollar-value tiers (FAR 6.303/6.304), and posted publicly within 14 days of award (30 days for urgency) under FAR 6.305. Basis: FAR text (recalled; acquisition.gov blocked; the GSA GitHub mirror was fetched but subpart files were not resolvable).
workflows.why_humans_review: Estimate, basis = the FAR exception list and deviation structure: A missing evidence 10% (market research, sources-sought responses); B factual classification 15% (does only one responsible source exist; is this a follow-on); C rule interpretation 10%; D conflict of authorities 5%; E true discretion 25-30% (urgency, public interest, industrial mobilisation); F commercial negotiation 10%; G one-off circumstances 20% (each J&A is by definition tied to one acquisition); H repeatable ambiguity settled prospectively 5-10% (class deviations, class J&As, standing nonavailability determinations). The prospective part already has a formal, published, numbered instrument (class deviation / class J&A), so the H residue is served.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: FAR 1.404 lets an agency head authorise class deviations affecting more than one contracting action; DoD publishes them as numbered, dated, superseding instruments (e.g., 2024-Oxxxx series); FAR itself is versioned by Federal Acquisition Circular, the GitHub mirror noting 'FAC 2025-06 October 1, 2025'.
settlement_loop_evidence.source_type: government repo (fetched for versioning; deviation text recalled, acquisition.gov blocked)
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: A class deviation is exactly a recorded, versioned, prospective settlement applied to all later similar actions; volume is low (dozens per year per agency) and the mechanism already exists in law and in contract-writing systems.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: FAR 6.305 requires each J&A for other-than-full-and-open competition to be posted publicly (SAM.gov) within 14 days after award, so every sole-source decision is already a published, provenance-bearing record.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Case-specific by design; later cases cite earlier J&As informally but the rule requires a fresh justification each time (G, not H).

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Buy American waivers (public interest, nonavailability, unreasonable cost) are posted individually for public comment on madeinamerica.gov under EO 14005; nonavailability determinations for listed articles apply prospectively.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Individual waivers are one-off; the FAR 25.104 nonavailable-articles list is the prospective class settlement and already exists as a maintained list.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: EU Directive 2014/24/EU Art. 32 enumerates closed grounds for negotiated procedure without prior publication (no suitable tenders, technical/artistic/exclusive rights, extreme urgency, additional deliveries, repetition) and Art. 84 requires an individual report; France's Code de la commande publique R2122-8 sets a bright-line below-threshold direct purchase (40,000 EUR HT).
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Grounds are legal categories interpreted by review bodies and the CJEU; contracting authorities document each case; the prospective settlement layer is case law and DAJ guidance, not an employer ledger.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: TED open data and eForms SDK (OP-TED) expose procedure-type codes for every EU notice, so recurrence of exception grounds is measurable, but no statistics were retrievable this session.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Data only; would support a base-rate study of how often the same exception ground recurs for the same buyer.

workflows.economic_pain: Protest and audit risk rather than review labour: GAO protests ~1,800/yr with ~half effective (unverified), OIG findings on inadequate J&As, EU infringement and single-bidder concerns. Cost per J&A: NOT FOUND; typical J&A drafting is a contracting-officer task measured in hours to days (estimate, no source).
workflows.existing_solutions: Contract-writing systems (PRISM, CON-IT, ConWrite, Unison), SAM.gov posting, agency deviation registers, EU eForms/TED, French PLACE/DAJ fiches techniques and OECP; GRC/audit tools. The prospective instrument (class deviation, class J&A, nonavailability list) already exists as a formal published document type, so H3 largely holds.
workflows.buyer_and_budget: Head of contracting activity / procurement policy office; public-sector budget cycles and long sales cycles; incumbents are contract-writing platforms.
workflows.regulatory_constraints: Statute requires written, approved, published justification per action; approval authority scales with dollar value; automation cannot remove the certifying contracting officer (H4).
workflows.notes: Procurement exceptions are dominated by one-off (G), discretion (E) and negotiation (F), and the repeatable part already has a formal versioned instrument. No exception-log volumes could be verified.

workflows.name: Employee expenses (contrast only): out-of-policy rates, auto-approval, Ramp/Expensify/Navan policy agents
workflows.decision_volume: Prior evidence: IPSA 82,787 claims with 18 not paid and 446 repaid (prior_evidence.md, regulator data from the earlier investigation). Vendor out-of-policy rates: NOT FOUND this session (ramp.com, navan.com, use.expensify.com blocked).
workflows.human_review_rate: Expensify Collect plan default: 'a $100 auto-approval threshold and 0% random audit percentage'; Control plan lets admins set a threshold under which 'Concierge can automatically approve reports that don't exceed a specific threshold and don't contain violations' and route 'a percentage of compliant reports for manual approval' (random audit). workflows.why_humans_review: Basis = Expensify rule catalogue (receipt thresholds, flag above amount, flag older than N days, prohibited line items, category/tag approvers) and prior IPSA coding: A missing evidence 30% (receipt, itemisation); B factual classification 20% (category, merchant type); C 10%; D 2%; E discretionary relief 25% (IPSA: 18 of 46 appeals were discretionary relief/exception); F 0%; G 8%; H 5-10%. evidence_against_thesis: H3 (already encoded): French social-law rules-as-code projects (OpenFisca-France, Urssaf mon-entreprise, Code du travail numérique Publicodes models) already capture settled interpretations as executable rules, citing circulaires and agency guidance in comments; the remaining gap is provenance hygiene, not a missing product (fetched: openfisca aides_logement.py, modele-social README, publicodes README).

Owner is the regulator, not the enterprise: the one typed, versioned, per-agreement settlement corpus found in this cluster (Code du travail numérique contributions with REDACTING->VALIDATED->PUBLISHED pipeline and answer types) is published free by the Direction générale du Travail; employer-side demand for a separate ledger is correspondingly reduced (fetched: SocialGouv/cdtn-admin).

H4 (humans must remain): ERISA appeals must be decided by a named fiduciary without deference; ADA accommodations require an individualised interactive process; FMLA certification review; J&As must be certified by a contracting officer and approved at dollar tiers. In every workflow here the law keeps a human on the decision even after precedent exists (regulation texts recalled; hosts blocked).

H6 (feature not product): Ramp's policy agent (prior evidence) and Expensify's auto-approve/random-audit settings show the loop shipping as a feature of the expense platform; HRSD/Workday knowledge articles and payroll configuration play the same role in HR and payroll.

Procurement exceptions are structurally G/E/F: each sole-source justification is tied to a single acquisition and must be freshly justified and published (FAR 6.303-6.305); the prospective instrument (class deviation, class J&A, nonavailability list) already exists as a formal numbered document at low volume.

Payroll ambiguity that matters (exemption status, award interpretation) is settled upstream by WHD opinion letters, the Fair Work Commission/Ombudsman and courts, and lands as payroll configuration; DOL's own calculator is arithmetic-only, confirming the interpretive step sits outside the payroll engine.

Expenses remain negative: Expensify's default is a $100 auto-approval threshold with 0% random audit on Collect; control is limits plus sampling, consistent with the prior IPSA finding that pre-payment checking prevents almost nothing.

No verified operational volumes for HR tier-2 escalation shares, benefit appeal counts, or exception-log sizes could be obtained this session; the absence is uncertainty, but it also means no positive quantitative evidence for the thesis was found in this cluster.

refuted.claim: Code du travail numérique contributions are 'typed, versioned, provenance-bearing, prospective settlement of repeatable ambiguity (category H) at national scale'.
refuted.why: The actual corpus is small and is a digest of agreement text, not a settlement of ambiguity. Fetched the published dataset @socialgouv/contributions-data 3.89.0 (Ministry of Labour npm package, May 2022, https://registry.npmjs.org/@socialgouv/contributions-data/-/contributions-data-3.89.0.tgz): 41 questions x 126 IDCC agreements = 4,870 per-agreement answers; 31.9% (1,555) simply state the agreement provides nothing or refers back to the Code; 69.4% carry a legifrance article citation, i.e. they summarise what an article says (e.g. 'Article 11: the employer must give preference to existing staff'). Cloned SocialGouv/cdtn-admin (release 2.77.12, 18 Sep 2026): the tracked generic-contribution list is 51 slugs (analysis/src/analysis/reports/completion_contributions.py, BASE_SLUGS) and the 'lot 2' migration references question order up to 51, so the corpus grew from 41 to about 51 recurring FAQ topics in four years. The REDACTING->PUBLISHED status table with user_id/created_at is an ordinary editorial CMS workflow, and the analytics module measures page views and 'afficher les informations' clicks, not questions escalated or settled. This is a government FAQ/knowledge base of type C at best (reading an existing text), not an H settlement loop, and its scale is ~50 topics, not 'national scale' of decisions.

manual_review_conflated_with_repeatable_: CDTN 'contributions' (HR, France): 51 FAQ topics answered per agreement by summarising the agreement's article, with 32% of answers being 'the agreement says nothing'. This is document lookup / editorial summarisation of an existing text (category C at most, largely deterministic reading), presented by the finder as H settlement. The editorial status pipeline is CMS workflow, not decision provenance. Re-estimate: of the human work behind CDTN, ~0% is H in the brief's sense; it is a knowledge-base authoring cost borne by the regulator.

ERISA (b)(5)/(g)(1)(v) 'internal rule, guideline, protocol' (benefits, US): these are clinical criteria and claims manuals applied to facts (medical necessity, disability definition met), i.e. category B with a disclosure duty; a consistency safeguard is not evidence that interpretive ambiguity recurs. Recalled KFF marketplace data (https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/issue-brief/claims-denials-and-appeals-in-aca-marketplace-plans-in-2023/, press/think-tank analysis of CMS PUF, unverified): ~19% of in-network claims denied, consumers appealed <1% of denials, insurers upheld ~56% on appeal, and the largest stated reasons are administrative/'other' and excluded service, not interpretation. Missing-facts and administrative categories (A) dominate; H re-estimated at ~0-5% of appeals, unknown share of which recurs.

Federal-sector discipline (Douglas factors): finder counts penalty consistency as H; it is E (individualised twelve-factor weighing) constrained by a pre-existing table of penalties (H3), with a human required on every case (H4).

Australian award interpretation: 'repeated across thousands of employees' is one misconfiguration replicated by software, not recurring human settlement; the fix is a court/FWC ruling plus payroll reconfiguration (regulator-owned settlement, H3). Employer-side H re-estimate: ~0-5% of payroll exceptions, likely settled once per award clause per employer.

Garnishment 'order interpretation' (payroll): priority and limits are statutory (CCPA limits, state priority rules) applied to the order document; the human work is A (obtaining and reading orders) and D resolved by fixed statutory rules, not H.

Procurement J&A drafting: each justification is statutorily per-action (G) with certification (H4); the recurring part (class J&A, class deviation, nonavailability list) is already a formal numbered instrument (H3). Employer-side H re-estimate: ~0-5%, already served.

FMLA/ADA determinations: the finder's H 10-15% has no case data; certification review (A), serious-health-condition and essential-function classification (B), undue hardship (E) and the mandatory interactive process (H4) dominate. Recurring employer-level interpretations (e.g., what counts as intermittent leave for a given role) are typically settled into leave-vendor eligibility configuration or HR knowledge articles (H3/H6). Re-estimate H ~0-5%.

verification.overall: The finder's structural narrative largely survives but its two positive-leaning items do not. Verified by fetch: the Expensify control model, the FAR deviation/J&A regime, the DOL timesheet scope, and the CDTN admin pipeline. Measured for the first time: the CDTN 'settlement corpus' is a government FAQ of ~41-51 topics answered per agreement by citing the agreement's article, a third of which say the agreement is silent; that is document lookup, not settlement of repeatable ambiguity, and its owner is the regulator. Benefits administration was over-graded on recalled regulation text and mis-scoped (health/disability rules generalised to all ERISA claims; clinical criteria treated as interpretive settlements); recalled base rates put appeals under 1% of denials with administrative reasons dominant, and every appeal keeps a human fiduciary.
